overview.intro:
Chapter 56 covers textile products made without weaving: **wadding** and flock (5601), **felt** (5602) and **nonwovens** (5603), special yarns — **rubber thread, metalized, gimped and chenille yarn** (5604–5606) — **twine, cordage and rope** (5607), knotted **netting and fishing nets** (5608) and articles of rope or cord (5609). Its **81 tariff lines** carry base rates from Free (all 27 nonwoven lines) to 14.1% on cotton hammocks, with compound rates on wool felt and some rope.

The extra duty by country decides the cost. Since **July 24, 2026** goods from 60 economies pay a **Section 301 tariff of 10% or 12.5%** (EU and Taiwanese goods 10%, Japanese and Korean 12.5% in total), and no country exception list except Jordan's — and Guatemala's and El Salvador's for CAFTA-DR goods — covers Chapter 56. **China pays 37.5%** extra on almost every line, Brazil up to 37.5%, and **Canada 50%** under Section 338 on most nonwovens and braided synthetic cordage, USMCA claim or not. U.S. imports were **$3.01B** in 2025; nonwovens were 68% of it and China the largest supplier (20%), ahead of Germany, India, Canada and Japan.

productGroups.label: Wadding, textile flock, dust and mill neps
productGroups.blurb: Wadding (batting) and articles of wadding of cotton (3.6%), man-made fibres (6.3%, including flocked swabs) or other fibres (4%), plus textile flock, dust and mill neps (Free). Sanitary pads, tampons and diapers made of wadding are heading 9619, not here.

productGroups.label: Felt, including needleloom felt and stitchbonded fabrics
productGroups.blurb: Felt. Needleloom felt and stitchbonded fabrics: 12% laminated, 10.6% other. Felt not impregnated or coated: wool 49.5¢/kg + 7.5%, other fibres 6.3%. Other felt: laminated Free, man-made fibres 6.3%, other 52.9¢/kg + 8%. These are the chapter's only compound rates on felt.

productGroups.label: Nonwovens (spunbond, meltblown, needlepunched, spunlace)
productGroups.blurb: Nonwovens of man-made filaments (spunbond, meltblown) or of staple fibres (spunlace, needlepunched, thermal bonded), split by weight per m². All 27 lines are Free at the general rate, so the extra duty by country is the whole cost.

productGroups.label: Rubber thread and cord, textile covered; coated or sheathed yarn
productGroups.blurb: Textile-covered rubber thread and cord (6.3%); high-tenacity polyester, nylon or viscose rayon yarn, impregnated or coated (8.8%); other yarn and strip impregnated, coated, covered or sheathed with rubber or plastics (5%).

productGroups.label: Metalized yarn
productGroups.blurb: Metalized yarn: metal-coated or metal-laminated man-made filament or strip, ungimped and untwisted (7.5%), and other yarn combined with metal thread, strip or powder or covered with metal (13.2%).

productGroups.label: Gimped yarn, chenille yarn and loop wale-yarn
productGroups.blurb: Gimped yarn and gimped strip, chenille yarn (including flock chenille) and loop wale-yarn: 8%, split by whether it contains elastomeric filaments.

productGroups.label: Twine, cordage, ropes and cables
productGroups.blurb: Twine, cordage, rope and cable by fibre: sisal baler twine Free; polyethylene and polypropylene 2.7% (wide strip) to 7%, or 9.8¢/kg + 5.3% for thick unbraided rope; nylon, polyester and other synthetics 3.6% braided, 7% or 19.9¢/kg + 10.8% unbraided; coir, jute and thick abaca Free; other abaca 3.4%; other fibres 6.3%.

productGroups.label: Knotted netting and made-up nets, including fishing nets
productGroups.blurb: Knotted netting of twine, cordage or rope and made-up nets: man-made fishing nets 8%, fish netting 8.5%, other man-made netting and nets (cargo nets, bait bags) 5%; nets of other materials: fishing 8%, cotton hammocks and netting 14.1% (the chapter's highest ad valorem rate), other 5%.

productGroups.label: Articles of yarn, twine, cordage or rope (n.e.s.)
productGroups.blurb: Articles of yarn, strip, twine, cordage, rope or cables not covered elsewhere (for example ropes with fittings and twist ties): 2.9% cotton, Free vegetable fibres, 4.5% man-made fibres, 3.9% other.

workedExamples.title: Spunbond polypropylene nonwoven from China
workedExamples.body: Filament nonwovens of 25–70 g/m² are Free at the general rate, but China pays 25% under List 3 (9903.88.03) and 12.5% under the 2026 action (9903.05.31). A $20,000 shipment pays **$7,500**. The same fabric from Mexico with a USMCA claim pays **$0**.

workedExamples.title: Spunbond nonwoven from Canada, with a USMCA claim
workedExamples.body: USMCA removes Canada's 10% Section 301 duty (9903.05.93), but 5603.12.00 is on the Canada Section 338 list (U.S. note 51(b)(3), 9903.03.14), and that 50% applies even when USMCA is claimed: **$10,000** on a $20,000 shipment entered since August 22, 2026. Filament nonwovens of 25 g/m² or less (5603.11) are not on the list and pay $0 with USMCA.

workedExamples.title: Staple-fibre nonwoven from China under the product exclusion
workedExamples.body: This statistical line is on the China exclusion list (U.S. note 20(vvv)(iii)(9), 9903.88.69) through November 9, 2026, so the 25% List 3 duty does not apply; the 12.5% (9903.05.31) does. A $10,000 shipment pays **$1,250** instead of $3,750.

workedExamples.title: Laminated needleloom felt from Germany
workedExamples.body: The base rate is 12%. EU goods pay the Section 301 rate as "10% in total in place of the base rate" (U.S. note 52(k), 9903.05.39), which only lifts rates below 10%, so this felt pays its 12% and nothing more: **$1,200** on a $10,000 shipment. German felt of other fibres at 6.3% (5602.29.00) pays 10% in total.

workedExamples.title: Sisal baler twine from Brazil
workedExamples.body: Binder or baler twine of sisal is Free, and it is the one Chapter 56 subheading on Brazil's exemption list (U.S. note 50(a)(ii), 9903.05.03), so it pays no 25% Brazil duty. It still pays the 12.5% 2026 action (9903.05.27): **$1,250** on a $10,000 shipment. Brazilian polypropylene twine (5607.41.30, 4%) pays 4% + 25% + 12.5% = 41.5%.

workedExamples.title: Thin polypropylene rope from Vietnam
workedExamples.body: Unbraided polyethylene or polypropylene rope under 4.8 mm is 7% at the general rate; Vietnam adds 12.5% (9903.05.84): **$1,950** on a $10,000 shipment. From India (+10%, 9903.05.44) it is $1,700.

notes.chapterNotes:
**Note 1.** Chapter 56 does not cover wadding, felt or nonwovens used merely as a carrier for perfumes, soaps, polishes or fabric softeners (chapters 33–38); quilted textile products of heading 5811; abrasive, mica or metal foil on a felt or nonwoven backing (6805, 6814, sections XIV–XV); or sanitary pads, tampons, diapers and diaper liners (heading 9619).

**Note 2.** "Felt" includes needleloom felt and fabrics whose web is stitch-bonded with fibres from the web itself.

**Note 3.** Headings 5602 and 5603 cover felt and nonwovens impregnated, coated, covered or laminated with plastics or rubber, and nonwovens bonded with plastics or rubber — but not felt with 50% or less textile by weight, or felt or nonwovens completely embedded in, or visibly coated on both sides with, plastics or rubber (chapters 39–40).

**Note 4.** Heading 5604 does not cover yarn or strip whose impregnation or coating cannot be seen with the naked eye (usually chapters 50–55).

**Section XI note 3.** Yarn is treated as "twine, cordage, ropes and cables" (heading 5607) when it measures more than 10,000 decitex if of man-made fibres, more than 20,000 decitex if of silk or of vegetable fibres other than true hemp or flax, 1,429 decitex or more if polished or glazed true hemp or flax, when it is coir of three or more plies, or when it is reinforced with metal thread. Wool yarn, paper yarn, man-made tow, monofilaments, metalized yarn (5605) and chenille or gimped yarn (5606) are never twine.
notes.additionalUsNotes:
**Additional U.S. note 1.** "Of wide nonfibrillated strip" (5607.41.10, 5607.49.10, 2.7%) means twine, cordage, rope or cable containing more than 65% by weight of nonfibrillated polyethylene or polypropylene strip more than 25.4 mm wide when unfolded.

**Additional U.S. note 2.** Heading 5607 does not cover twine, cordage, rope or cable of metal (section XV).

**Statistical note 1.** "Salmon gill netting" (5608.19.10.10) is double- or triple-knot nylon fish netting of fine monofilament or multifilament yarn with a stretch mesh of 10.5–21.6 cm.

The three-digit numbers in brackets (201, 223, 229, 369, 414, 469, 669, 899) are textile category numbers used to monitor shipments.

tariffUpdates.h1: HTS Chapter 56 Tariff Updates 2026: Nonwovens, Felt, Twine & Rope

seo.title: HTS Chapter 56 Tariff Updates 2026: Section 301 on Nonwovens, Canada 338, China Lists, IEEPA End | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: What changed for HTS Chapter 56 imports since January 2025: unchanged base rates, the end of the IEEPA tariffs and the Section 122 surcharge, the 2026 Section 301 tariffs, China List 3 and its nonwoven exclusions, Canada's 50% Section 338 duty on nonwovens and AD/CVD on twist ties.

tariffUpdates.intro:
This page compares two editions of the tariff schedule: the **2025 Basic Edition**, in force at the start of 2025, and the current **2026 Revision 21** (in force October 9, 2026). All 81 Chapter 56 lines carry the same base rates in both.

What changed came on top of the base rate. The 2025 IEEPA duties — up to 50% on Indian goods — **ended on February 24, 2026**, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge that replaced them expired on July 23, 2026. Since **July 24, 2026**, goods from 60 economies pay a **Section 301 tariff of 10% or 12.5%**, with no exception list for Chapter 56 except Jordan's and the CAFTA-DR lists. China keeps its 25% List 3 duty, Brazil pays another 25% (sisal baler twine excepted), and since **August 22, 2026 Canada pays 50%** under Section 338 on most nonwovens and braided synthetic cordage. China's exclusions for three staple-fibre nonwoven lines expire after November 9, 2026.
tariffUpdates.scope: Measures that reach Chapter 56 from any country: the 2026 Section 301 tariffs on 60 economies and their exception lists, the Brazil Section 301 tariff, China Section 301 List 3 and its nonwoven exclusions, the Canada Section 338 duty, the Nicaragua Section 301 phase-in, the 2025–2026 IEEPA and Section 122 duties that have ended, and the antidumping and countervailing duty orders on twist ties and plastic decorative ribbon from China that name heading 5609 numbers. No Section 232 heading lists a Chapter 56 provision. For the rate each supplier pays, see Rates by country.

inEffect.exemption: List 3 (+25%, 9903.88.03, 25% since May 10, 2019) covers every Chapter 56 subheading, and the 2026 action adds +12.5% (9903.05.31); China is on no 2026 exception list. Product exclusions (U.S. note 20(vvv)(iii)(9)–(10), 9903.88.69) remove the 25% from three staple-fibre nonwoven lines (5603.92.00.70, 5603.92.00.95 and 5603.93.00.90) through November 9, 2026; they do not lift the 12.5%. USTR confirmed on October 7, 2026 that the 2018 actions continue. AD/CVD orders on twist ties and plastic decorative ribbon from China can apply to goods entered under 5609. The IEEPA duties on China ended February 24, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Chinese nonwovens, wadding, rope, twine and nets pay 37.5% on top of the base rate — up to 51.6% on cotton hammocks; the three excluded nonwoven lines pay 12.5% until November 9, 2026.

inEffect.exemption: EU goods pay 10% in total in place of the base rate (U.S. note 52(k), 9903.05.39). The EU exception list (U.S. note 52(j)(2), 9903.05.97) names no Chapter 56 subheading. Lines whose base rate is above 10% — needleloom felt (10.6%, 12%), metalized yarn (13.2%), cotton hammocks and netting (14.1%) and usually the compound felt rates — pay only the base rate. The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: German, Dutch, Luxembourg and French nonwovens — Germany alone shipped $222.1M in 2025 — pay 10% in total; needleloom felt pays its own 10.6% or 12%.

inEffect.exemption: India has no exception list. GSP (SPI A), printed on six rope and netting subheadings, has been expired since December 31, 2020. The 2025 IEEPA duties (25% reciprocal plus 25% over Russian oil purchases) ended in February 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Indian nonwovens, rope and chenille yarn pay the base rate plus 10%: 10% on nonwovens, 17% on thin polypropylene rope.

inEffect.exemption: USMCA-qualifying goods pay no Section 301 duty (9903.05.93), but the 50% Section 338 duty (U.S. note 51(b)(3), 9903.03.14) on man-made-filament nonwovens over 25 g/m² (5603.12, 5603.13, 5603.14.90), staple-fibre nonwovens of 25–70 g/m² and over 150 g/m² (5603.92, 5603.94.90) and braided synthetic cordage (5607.50.40) applies with or without a USMCA claim. Proclamation 11065 (September 15, 2026) neither added nor removed a Chapter 56 provision, and no Chapter 56 line is on the September 29, 2026 import-ban annexes. The IEEPA duty on Canada ended February 24, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Canadian nonwovens on the Section 338 list pay 50% even with USMCA (60% without); Canadian felt, wadding, most rope and light filament nonwovens pay nothing extra with USMCA and the base rate plus 10% without.

inEffect.exemption: Japan's rate is 12.5% in total in place of the base rate (U.S. note 52(k), 9903.05.49); Japan has no exception list. Only the compound wool-felt rates can exceed it, depending on weight. The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Japanese nonwovens — $177.0M in 2025, nearly all of Japan's Chapter 56 trade — pay 12.5% in total.

inEffect.exemption: USMCA-qualifying goods pay no Section 301 duty (9903.05.94). Under the Chapter 56 rules of General Note 11, the goods may not be made from non-originating man-made filaments or fibres (chapters 54–55) or non-originating wool, cotton or vegetable-fibre yarn and fabric. The 2025 IEEPA duty on Mexico (+25%, 9903.01.01) ended February 24, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Mexican nonwovens, wadding, rope and felt pay $0 with a valid USMCA claim and the base rate plus 10% without one.

inEffect.exemption: Türkiye has no exception list for Chapter 56; its rate is the base rate plus 12.5% (9903.05.79). The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Turkish nonwovens ($125.2M in 2025) pay 12.5%, and wadding 12.5%–18.8%.

inEffect.exemption: South Korea's rate is 12.5% in total in place of the base rate (U.S. note 52(k), 9903.05.71), KORUS claim or not; every Chapter 56 KORUS rate is Free. Korea has no exception list. The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Korean nonwovens and every other Chapter 56 good pay 12.5% in total.

inEffect.exemption: Vietnam has no exception list for Chapter 56; its rate is the base rate plus 12.5% (9903.05.84). The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Vietnamese rope and twine — Vietnam's largest Chapter 56 product — pay 12.5% to 19.5%, and 19.9¢/kg + 23.3% on unbraided synthetic rope.

inEffect.exemption: Thailand has no exception list for Chapter 56; its rate is the base rate plus 12.5% (9903.05.77). GSP has been expired since December 31, 2020. The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Thai nonwovens pay 12.5%, wadding 12.5%–18.8% and needleloom felt up to 24.5%.

inEffect.exemption: The UK exception list (U.S. note 52(j)(1), 9903.05.96) names no Chapter 56 subheading, so British goods pay the base rate plus 10% (9903.05.81). The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: British rope and nonwovens pay the base rate plus 10%.

inEffect.exemption: Taiwan's rate is 10% in total in place of the base rate (U.S. note 52(k), 9903.05.76); its exception list names no Chapter 56 subheading. The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Taiwanese nonwovens pay 10% in total; lines with a base rate above 10% pay only the base rate.

inEffect.exemption: Israel pays the base rate plus 12.5% (9903.05.47). The U.S.–Israel FTA (SPI IL) removes the base rate but not the Section 301 duty (U.S. note 52(a)). The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Israeli nonwovens ($42.7M in 2025, almost all of Israel's Chapter 56 trade) pay 12.5%.

inEffect.exemption: Brazil's 25% (9903.05.01, from July 22, 2026) reaches every Chapter 56 line except sisal or agave binder and baler twine (5607.21.00), which is on Brazil's exemption list (U.S. note 50(a)(ii), 9903.05.03). The 2026 action adds 12.5% (9903.05.27) on every line. The 2025 IEEPA duties (10% reciprocal and 40%) ended February 24, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Brazilian sisal baler twine pays 12.5%; other Brazilian rope and goods pay 37.5% on top of the base rate. Twine and rope were $26.6M of Brazil's $30.4M in 2025.

inEffect.country: Other Section 301 economies (45: Algeria, Angola, Argentina, Australia, Bahamas, Bahrain, Bangladesh, Cambodia, …)
inEffect.exemption: Exception lists in U.S. note 52(j) cover every Chapter 56 subheading for Jordan (9903.06.20) and, for goods entered under CAFTA-DR, Guatemala and El Salvador (9903.06.06, 9903.06.09). CAFTA-DR textile goods of Costa Rica, the Dominican Republic, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras and Nicaragua entered duty-free under CAFTA-DR are exempt (note 52(i), 9903.05.95). No other country list names a Chapter 56 code. The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Most other suppliers pay the base rate plus 10% or 12.5%; Jordanian goods and CAFTA-DR textiles enter at the base rate (usually Free under the agreement).

changes.title: No Chapter 56 base-rate changes
changes.detail: All 81 Chapter 56 lines carry the same General, FTA and Column 2 rates in the 2026 Revision 21 as in the 2025 Basic Edition; no line was added, split or renumbered.

changes.title: China nonwoven exclusions expire after November 9, 2026
changes.detail: The Section 301 product exclusions for staple-fibre nonwovens of 25–70 g/m² (5603.92.00.70, 5603.92.00.95) and 70–150 g/m² (5603.93.00.90) from China (U.S. note 20(vvv)(iii)(9)–(10), 9903.88.69) run through November 9, 2026. Unless USTR extends them again, these lines pay the 25% List 3 duty again from November 10, on top of the 12.5%.

changes.title: China Section 301 List 3 continues
changes.detail: USTR received requests to continue the 2018 China Section 301 actions, so they stay in effect during the four-year review. For Chapter 56 this keeps +25% (9903.88.03) on every subheading, from wadding and felt to rope and nets.

changes.title: Canadian import bans do not reach Chapter 56
changes.detail: Proclamations 11061–11063 banned some Canadian alcoholic beverages, dairy-scope products and motorcycles from September 29, 2026. No Chapter 56 line is on their annexes, so Canadian nonwovens and cordage still enter, paying the 50% Section 338 duty where listed.

changes.title: Section 338 list revised; Chapter 56 nonwovens stay on it
changes.detail: Proclamation 11065 added and deleted products on the 9903.03.14 list from September 15, 2026. It neither added nor removed a Chapter 56 provision: Revision 21 still lists 5603.12.00, 5603.13.00, 5603.14.90, 5603.92.00, 5603.94.90 and 5607.50.40 in U.S. note 51(b)(3).

changes.title: Canada Section 338 duty of 50% on most nonwovens and braided synthetic cordage
changes.detail: Proclamation 11048 put a 50% duty (9903.03.14) on Canadian goods in the provisions of U.S. note 51(b)(3). In Chapter 56 that is 5603.12.00, 5603.13.00, 5603.14.90, 5603.92.00, 5603.94.90 and 5607.50.40 — 17 of 81 lines. It is charged even when USMCA is claimed and on top of the 10% Section 301 duty on non-USMCA goods. Planned for August 19, it took effect August 22 after a 3-day suspension (Proclamation 11056).

changes.title: Section 301 tariffs on 60 economies reach every Chapter 56 line
changes.detail: 10% or 12.5% on all products of 60 economies (9903.05.20–9903.05.84). No Chapter 56 subheading is on the general exemption list (note 52(b)) or on the EU, UK, Swiss, Japanese or Korean exception lists; only Jordan's list covers the whole chapter, and Guatemala's and El Salvador's lists cover it for goods entered under CAFTA-DR. EU and Taiwanese goods pay 10% and Japanese, Korean and Swiss goods 12.5% in total, in place of a lower base rate; USMCA-qualifying goods are exempt (9903.05.93, 9903.05.94). FTA claims remove the base rate but not this duty.

changes.title: Section 122 import surcharge expired
changes.detail: The 150-day surcharge (9903.03.01) expired at the close of July 23, 2026.

changes.title: Section 301 tariff on products of Brazil
changes.detail: 25% on all goods of Brazil (9903.05.01). Brazil's exemption list (U.S. note 50(a)(ii), 9903.05.03) names one Chapter 56 subheading, sisal and agave binder or baler twine (5607.21.00). From July 24 the 12.5% 2026 action (9903.05.27) is added on top, including on baler twine.

changes.title: USMCA joint review: not renewed, still in force
changes.detail: The United States did not agree to renew the USMCA in its current form. USTR said the Agreement remains in force pending resolution of the issues or until termination, so USMCA claims (SPI S) still apply.

changes.title: Twist ties from China: AD/CVD orders likely to continue
changes.detail: Commerce's expedited sunset reviews found that revoking the antidumping and countervailing duty orders on twist ties from China (A-570-131, C-570-132) would likely lead to dumping margins up to 72.96% and subsidy rates of 111.96%. The orders name 5609.00.30.00 as a primary entry number. The ITC decided on June 5, 2026 to conduct full five-year reviews; the orders stay in force until it decides.

changes.title: CBP forced-labor guidance: cotton tracing applies to cotton wadding
changes.detail: CBP's operational guidance for importers lists supply-chain tracing documents for the UFLPA high-priority sectors, including cotton and cotton products. Cotton wadding (5601.21) and cotton netting, hammocks and cordage articles fall under the cotton guidance; the UFLPA presumption applies to goods of any kind made wholly or in part in Xinjiang or by a listed entity.

changes.title: Section 122 surcharge replaces the IEEPA tariffs
changes.detail: 10% on products of all countries (9903.03.01) until July 23, 2026. No Chapter 56 subheading was on the product exemption list (9903.03.03). USMCA-qualifying goods from Canada and Mexico were exempt (9903.03.07, 9903.03.08).

changes.title: All IEEPA tariffs end
changes.detail: After the Supreme Court held on February 20, 2026 (Learning Resources, Inc. v. Trump) that IEEPA does not authorize tariffs, Executive Order 14389 ended the Canada, Mexico, China, Brazil, India and reciprocal duties, and CBP stopped collecting them for goods entered from 12:00 a.m. ET on February 24. The 9903.01.xx and 9903.02.xx headings are still printed in Revision 21 but are no longer in effect.

changes.title: India's extra 25% IEEPA duty removed
changes.detail: Executive Order 14384 ended the additional 25% duty on products of India (9903.01.84) from February 7, 2026. India's 25% reciprocal rate ended with the other IEEPA duties on February 24.

changes.title: AGOA reauthorized through December 31, 2026
changes.detail: The Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026 renewed AGOA retroactively from September 30, 2025. AGOA (SPI D) is printed on six Chapter 56 subheadings — 5607.29.00, 5607.41.10, 5607.49.10, 5607.90.35, 5608.90.23 and 5608.90.30. GSP (SPI A), printed on the same six, remains expired since December 31, 2020.

changes.title: Nicaragua Section 301 tariff phases in from 2027
changes.detail: USTR's action on Nicaragua adds a duty on all Nicaraguan goods that do not originate under CAFTA-DR (9903.89.01): 0% in 2026, 10% from January 1, 2027 and 15% from January 1, 2028. It reaches every Chapter 56 line.

changes.title: China nonwoven exclusions extended to November 9, 2026
changes.detail: USTR extended all 178 China Section 301 exclusions under 9903.88.69, including three nonwoven statistical lines of staple fibres (5603.92.00.70, 5603.92.00.95 and 5603.93.00.90). They remove the 25% List 3 duty, not the 12.5% 2026 action.

changes.title: China fentanyl duty cut to 10%
changes.detail: The IEEPA duty on products of China and Hong Kong (9903.01.24) fell from +20% to +10%. It applied to every Chapter 56 line on top of the 25% List 3 duty until it ended on February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Extra 25% on products of India
changes.detail: Executive Order 14329 added 25% on Indian goods (9903.01.84) over India's purchases of Russian oil, on top of the 25% reciprocal rate in force since August 7, 2025 (EO 14326): 50% in all on Indian twine, rope, felt and nonwovens. Ended February 7, 2026.

changes.title: Country-specific reciprocal rates
changes.detail: Executive Order 14326 replaced the 10% baseline with country rates, for example India +25%, Vietnam and Taiwan +20%, Japan and South Korea +15%, and 15% in total for EU goods. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: 40% IEEPA duty on products of Brazil
changes.detail: Executive Order 14323 (signed July 30, 2025) added 40% on goods of Brazil (9903.01.77), on top of the 10% reciprocal duty. Its exemption list (9903.01.81) included sisal baler twine (5607.21.00). Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Canada additional duty raised to 35%
changes.detail: Raised the IEEPA duty on non-USMCA Canadian goods to +35% (9903.01.10). Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Reciprocal tariff on products of all countries
changes.detail: 10% baseline (9903.01.25) and country rates (9903.02.xx); Canada and Mexico excluded. No Chapter 56 subheading was on the general exemption list. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: China fentanyl duty raised to 20%
changes.detail: The IEEPA duty on products of China and Hong Kong (9903.01.20, then 9903.01.24) went from +10% (from February 4, 2025) to +20%, on top of the 25% List 3 duty on Chapter 56 goods.

changes.title: Additional duty on products of Mexico
changes.detail: +25% on non-USMCA goods (9903.01.01); USMCA-qualifying goods exempt (9903.01.04). Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Additional duty on products of Canada
changes.detail: +25% on non-USMCA goods (9903.01.10), later raised to +35%; USMCA-qualifying goods exempt (9903.01.14). Ended February 24, 2026.

understandIndustry.why:
U.S. imports of Chapter 56 goods were **$3.01B in 2025**, -1.7% against $3.06B in 2024 and below the 2021 peak of $3.41B. **China** stayed the largest supplier at **$604.0M** (-12.6%), but its share has fallen from 32% in 2020 to 20%. **Germany $253.3M** (+8%), **India $226.9M**, **Canada $203.1M**, **Japan $197.1M** and **Mexico $176.8M** follow; **South Korea** grew fastest of the top ten (+24%).

**Nonwovens are the trade**: heading 5603 was $2.04B, 68% of the total, led by spunbond and meltblown filament nonwovens of 25–70 g/m² (5603.12, $478.5M). Twine and rope (5607) were $321.8M, wadding (5601) $192.4M, rope articles (5609) $154.9M — nearly half from China — and felt (5602) $119.1M, where Canada is the largest supplier. Vietnam ships mainly rope and nonwovens, Brazil almost only twine and rope.

Through 2025 most suppliers paid the IEEPA tariffs — 50% on Indian goods from August 27 — on top of the base rate, and China its 25% List 3 duty as well. The IEEPA duties ended on February 24, 2026; since July 24, 2026 a Section 301 tariff of 10% or 12.5% applies instead, and since August 22 Canadian nonwovens on the Section 338 list pay 50%. 2025 is the latest full year of U.S. trade data.

industryAreas.intro:
The total rate on a Chapter 56 good depends far more on **where it comes from** than on what it is. Each cell below is the base rate for that product group plus the extra duty for that country, minus any preference — computed from the current tariff schedule with the same engine as the tariff calculator.

Since the IEEPA duties ended on February 24, 2026, the extra duty is mainly the **Section 301 tariff on 60 economies** (from July 24, 2026). **EU and Taiwanese goods pay 10% in total** and **Japan and South Korea 12.5% in total**, in place of a lower base rate; **India and the UK add 10%**, **Türkiye, Vietnam, Thailand and Israel 12.5%**. **China and Brazil pay 37.5% more** on almost every line, and **Canada pays 50%** on most nonwovens and braided synthetic cordage even with USMCA. Mexican goods that qualify for USMCA pay nothing.

EU, Taiwanese, Japanese and Korean rates of "10% / 12.5% in total" replace the base rate only when it is lower (U.S. note 52(k)); needleloom felt, metalized yarn and cotton hammocks keep their higher base rate.
China's nonwoven exclusions (5603.92.00.70, 5603.92.00.95 and 5603.93.00.90) cover whole statistical lines, so the China cells apply them (12.5% instead of 37.5%); they expire after November 9, 2026.
Canada: the 50% Section 338 duty (U.S. note 51) applies whether or not USMCA is claimed; no Chapter 56 line is on the September 29, 2026 import-ban annexes.

CAFTA-DR textile goods (note 52(i), 9903.05.95) and Jordanian goods (9903.06.20) are exempt from the Section 301 duty; they fall in "Any other country". Myanmar's imports have no ISO code in the trade data and are counted there too.

Not in the grid: antidumping and countervailing duties on Chinese twist ties and plastic decorative ribbon entered under 5609, the UFLPA presumption against goods made in Xinjiang, and textile entry rules — see Import documents.

tariffEngineering.h1: Importing Nonwovens, Felt, Rope & Netting (HTS Ch. 56): Origin Rules, Documents & Ways to Lower Duty

seo.title: Importing Nonwovens, Rope & Twine: Textile Origin, FTC Labeling, UFLPA & Duty Savings (HTS Chapter 56) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: The CBP, FTC and FDA rules for each HTS Chapter 56 line — textile country of origin (19 CFR 102.21), manufacturer ID, invoice and fibre-content labeling, UFLPA, AD/CVD on twist ties — and the legal ways to pay less: USMCA, CAFTA-DR, the China nonwoven exclusion, rulings, samples and drawback.

tariffEngineering.intro:
Chapter 56 goods are textiles, so **CBP's textile rules decide their origin**: nonwovens and felt are from where the web was formed, rope and twine from where the filaments were extruded or the fibres spun, and made-up nets from where the netting was made or the net assembled (19 CFR 102.21). Every entry names the manufacturer through a manufacturer identification code, and goods made wholly or in part in Xinjiang are presumed barred under the UFLPA.

The ways to pay less are in the schedule: claim **USMCA** on North American goods (it removes the 10% Section 301 duty but not Canada's 50% Section 338 duty on listed nonwovens), claim **CAFTA-DR** for Central American textiles, use **China's nonwoven exclusion** while it lasts, get a **ruling** where weight per m², fibre or construction decides the line, enter **samples** under Chapter 98, and claim **drawback** on re-exports. Each depends on a document, listed below with its regulation.

levers.title: Claim USMCA on nonwovens, felt, yarn, rope or nets made in Mexico or Canada
levers.saves: The 10% Section 301 duty for Mexico or Canada plus the base rate (up to 14.1%, or the compound felt and rope rates)
levers.appliesTo: All 81 lines, for goods that qualify as originating: made in North America from fibres or yarn that are not non-originating man-made filaments or fibres (chapters 54–55) or non-originating wool, cotton or vegetable-fibre yarn and fabric (General Note 11, Chapter 56 rules)
levers.document: A certification of origin from the importer, exporter or producer, in any format, with the SPI "S" on the entry line.
levers.caveat: For Canada, USMCA does not remove the 50% Section 338 duty on 5603.12.00, 5603.13.00, 5603.14.90, 5603.92.00, 5603.94.90 and 5607.50.40. The USMCA was not renewed at the July 1, 2026 joint review but remains in force.

levers.title: Source CAFTA-DR or Jordanian textiles that are exempt from the Section 301 duty
levers.saves: The 10%–12.5% Section 301 duty, and the base rate where the FTA rate is Free
levers.appliesTo: Every Chapter 56 line from Jordan (U.S. note 52(j), 9903.06.20); every line from Guatemala and El Salvador entered under CAFTA-DR (9903.06.06, 9903.06.09); CAFTA-DR textile goods of Costa Rica, the Dominican Republic, Honduras and Nicaragua entered duty-free under CAFTA-DR (note 52(i), 9903.05.95)
levers.document: Proof of origin under the agreement and the SPI (P or P+ for CAFTA-DR, JO for Jordan) with the exemption heading on the entry line.
levers.caveat: The goods must originate under the agreement's textile rules, which generally require regional yarn or fibre. A CAFTA-DR claim also keeps Nicaraguan goods out of the 2027 Nicaragua Section 301 duty.

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. note 52(i), (j)

levers.title: Claim the China product exclusion for listed staple-fibre nonwovens
levers.saves: The 25% List 3 duty (the 12.5% 2026 duty still applies)
levers.appliesTo: Chinese nonwovens of staple fibres classified in 5603.92.00.70, 5603.92.00.95 and 5603.93.00.90, entered by November 9, 2026
levers.document: Heading 9903.88.69 reported with the excluded statistical number.
levers.caveat: The exclusion is tied to those statistical numbers; impregnated or coated nonwovens (.10 lines) and filament nonwovens (5603.1x) pay the full 37.5%. It ends after November 9, 2026 unless USTR extends it again.

levers.title: Claim an FTA or AGOA rate where the base rate is the cost
levers.saves: The base rate: up to 14.1% (cotton hammocks and netting), 13.2% (metalized yarn), 12% (laminated needleloom felt), 10.6% (other needleloom felt), 8.5% (fish netting), 8% (fishing nets, gimped yarn) and the compound felt and rope rates
levers.appliesTo: The 47 dutiable lines, for goods of Korea, Australia, Chile, Colombia, Peru, Panama, Israel, Morocco, Bahrain, Oman and Singapore; AGOA countries (through December 31, 2026) only on 5607.29, 5607.41.10, 5607.49.10, 5607.90.35, 5608.90.23 and 5608.90.30
levers.document: Proof of origin under the agreement and the SPI on the entry line (KR, AU, CL, CO, PE, PA, IL, MA, BH, OM, SG, D).
levers.caveat: FTA claims do not remove the 2026 Section 301 duty (U.S. note 52(a)); Korea's 12.5% applies in total whatever the KORUS rate. GSP (A) has been expired since December 31, 2020. The Automotive Products Trade Act (B) applies only to original motor-vehicle equipment from Canada.

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. note 52(a)

levers.title: Get a binding classification ruling where weight, fibre or construction decides the line
levers.saves: Up to 14.1 points of base rate, and certainty for exclusion and Section 338 claims: nonwoven (Free) vs. felt (6.3%–12%) vs. coated fabric of chapter 59; filament vs. staple-fibre nonwoven and weight per m² (which decides the China exclusion and the Canada list); yarn vs. twine by decitex (Section XI note 3); braided vs. unbraided rope; knotted netting (5608) vs. knitted or tulle netting (6003, 5804)
levers.appliesTo: Any line where the material, weight per m², bonding, coating or construction is in doubt
levers.document: A ruling request to CBP describing fibre content by weight, construction, weight per m² or decitex and any coating (19 CFR part 177); invoices must state the same details (19 CFR 141.89).
levers.caveat: Rulings apply to the transaction described; a different blend, weight or coating may need its own.

citations.label: HTSUS Section XI notes (printed with Chapter 50)

levers.title: Declare the first-sale price when goods pass through a middleman
levers.saves: Duty on the middleman's markup — every ad valorem duty, including Section 301 and Section 338, is charged on the transaction value
levers.appliesTo: All lines bought through a trading company or agent, when the factory's sale to the middleman was for export to the United States
levers.document: The factory's invoice to the middleman and proof the sale was destined for the U.S. at the time (purchase orders, shipping documents), filed with the entry.
levers.caveat: The earlier sale must be a bona fide arm's-length sale for export to the U.S.; CBP may ask for the whole chain of documents.

levers.title: Enter swatches and sample cuts as samples
levers.saves: All duty — base rate and the Section 301, China and Canada duties
levers.appliesTo: Nonwoven, felt and netting swatches and rope samples valued at $1 or less each, or marked, torn or perforated so they cannot be sold, used only to solicit orders
levers.document: Entry under 9811.00.60 with the samples marked or mutilated as the heading requires.
levers.caveat: Usable cuts or sample rolls for production do not qualify. U.S. notes 20, 51 and 52 exempt goods properly entered under Chapter 98 from those extra duties.

provisions.text: Samples valued not over $1 each, or marked, torn, perforated or otherwise treated so they are unsuitable for sale, used only for soliciting orders for products of foreign countries

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. notes 20(a), 51, 52(a)

levers.title: Claim drawback when the goods, or what they are made into, are exported
levers.saves: Up to 99% of the duties paid, including Section 301 duties, on imported nonwovens, felt, yarn or rope re-exported or used in exported goods
levers.appliesTo: All lines, when the imported goods or substitutes are exported or used in manufacturing exported goods
levers.document: A drawback claim filed in ACE within 5 years of import, with records linking the import to the export.
levers.caveat: Only duties actually paid are refunded; manufacturing drawback needs a ruling or a general manufacturing ruling.

rules.title: Textile country of origin: felt and nonwovens from where a fabric-making process formed them (or where greige goods were both dyed and printed with two more finishing operations); special yarn (5604–5606), twine and rope from where the filaments were extruded or the fibres spun; knotted netting from where it was made, and nets with non-textile attachments from where they were wholly assembled; 5609 articles from where the filaments were extruded or the fibres spun; wadding by a change of heading that excludes staple fibres of 5105, 5203 and 5501–5507
Manufacturer identification code (MID) of the company that performed the origin-conferring operation on every entry — this replaced the textile declaration, eliminated in 2011
Entry is denied for textiles from a company named by CITA in the Federal Register for illegal transshipment or for being unable to verify production
Invoice details for textile fibre products: each fibre by generic name and percentage by weight, in order of predominance; for yarns, single or plied and whether put up for retail sale

Textile Fiber Products Identification Act: batts, yarns, fabrics (including felt and nonwoven fabric) and hammocks sold onward must show fibre content and the country where processed or made; disposable nonwovens for one-time use and products not on the covered list (such as rope, twine and nets) are excluded

UFLPA: goods made wholly or in part in Xinjiang or by an entity on the UFLPA Entity List are presumed made with forced labor and excluded unless the importer rebuts it; cotton wadding and other cotton goods fall under CBP's cotton tracing guidance
Antidumping and countervailing duty orders on twist ties from China (A-570-131, C-570-132) name 5609.00.30.00; Chinese twist ties entered here need the AD/CVD case numbers and cash deposits
Antidumping and countervailing duty orders on plastic decorative ribbon from China (A-570-075, C-570-076) list 5609.00.30.00 and 5609.00.40.00 among the numbers the ribbon may enter under
Flocked swabs sold for medical specimen collection are FDA-regulated devices (Class I); the foreign establishment must register and list the device
Country-of-origin marking on the article or, for bulk rolls, coils and bales, on its container

groups.label: Wadding, textile flock, dust and mill neps
groups.note: Wadding changes origin by a change of heading, but not from carded or combed staple fibres (5105, 5203, 5501–5507); articles of wadding, flock and neps change origin even from wadding. Flocked swabs for specimen collection are FDA devices. Cotton wadding is a UFLPA cotton product.

groups.label: Felt, including needleloom felt and stitchbonded fabrics
groups.note: Felt takes the origin of the country where a fabric-making process formed it. Wool felt carries compound rates (49.5¢/kg + 7.5%, 52.9¢/kg + 8%), so invoices must state net weight.

groups.label: Nonwovens (spunbond, meltblown, needlepunched, spunlace)
groups.note: Nonwovens take the origin of the country where a fabric-making process formed the web. Weight per m² and filament vs. staple decide the line, the China exclusion (5603.92.00.70/.95, 5603.93.00.90) and the Canada Section 338 list. Disposable one-time-use nonwovens are outside FTC labeling.

groups.label: Rubber thread and cord, textile covered; coated or sheathed yarn
groups.note: Coated or covered yarn takes the origin of the country where the textile filaments were extruded or the fibres spun, not where they were coated.

groups.label: Metalized yarn
groups.note: Metalized yarn takes the origin of the country where the filaments were extruded or the fibres spun.

groups.label: Gimped yarn, chenille yarn and loop wale-yarn
groups.note: Gimped and chenille yarn take the origin of the country where the filaments were extruded or the fibres spun.

groups.label: Twine, cordage, ropes and cables
groups.note: Twine and rope take the origin of the country where the filaments or strip were extruded or the fibres spun — twisting or braiding imported yarn does not change it. Braided synthetic cordage (5607.50.40) is on Canada's Section 338 list; sisal baler twine is on Brazil's exemption list.

groups.label: Knotted netting and made-up nets, including fishing nets
groups.note: Netting takes the origin of the country where it was knotted; nets with non-textile attachments, of the country where they were wholly assembled. Hammocks are on the FTC covered list.

groups.label: Articles of yarn, twine, cordage or rope (n.e.s.)
groups.note: Articles of yarn, twine or rope take the origin of the country where the filaments were extruded or the fibres spun. Chinese twist ties and plastic decorative ribbon entered here can be subject to AD/CVD orders.

tariffEngineering.disclaimer: A checklist of where the rules are, with links to the regulations — not legal advice. Exception lists, the China exclusions, the Canada Section 338 list and AD/CVD scopes change by proclamation and notice; check them before each shipment.

finalConclusion.h1: HTS Chapter 56 FAQ: Nonwoven, Rope, Twine & Felt HS Codes and Import Tariffs

seo.title: Nonwoven, Rope & Twine HS Code FAQ 2026: Felt, Wadding, Fishing Net Tariffs (HTS Chapter 56) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: Answers to what people search about HTS Chapter 56: the HS code for nonwoven fabric, rope, twine, felt, wadding, fishing nets, elastic cord and chenille yarn, and the 2026 tariffs on nonwovens from China and Canada.

finalConclusion.intro: Straight answers to the most common questions about importing Chapter 56 goods into the U.S. — HS codes, tariffs by country and entry rules. Each answer links to the page with the full detail.
keyTakeaways: Chapter 56 base rates are unchanged since January 2025: Free on 34 of 81 lines, including all 27 nonwoven lines, and up to 14.1% (cotton hammocks), with compound rates on wool felt and some rope.

Since July 24, 2026 nearly every supplier pays a 10% or 12.5% Section 301 tariff; no EU, UK, Japanese or Korean exception list covers Chapter 56. EU and Taiwanese goods pay 10% and Japanese and Korean 12.5% in total.

China pays 37.5% extra on almost every line (12.5% on three staple-fibre nonwoven lines excluded through November 9, 2026); Brazil 37.5% except sisal baler twine (12.5%); Canada 50% under Section 338 on most nonwovens and braided synthetic cordage, even with USMCA.
The IEEPA tariffs ended February 24, 2026 and the Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.

These are textiles: origin follows 19 CFR 102.21 (a nonwoven is from where its web was formed, rope from where its fibres were spun or extruded), every entry needs a manufacturer ID, and the UFLPA presumption bars goods made in Xinjiang.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for nonwoven fabric?
faqs.answer: Heading 5603. Nonwovens of man-made filaments — spunbond and meltblown polypropylene or polyester — are 5603.11 to 5603.14, split by weight: 25 g/m² or less, 25–70, 70–150 and over 150 g/m². Nonwovens of staple fibres, including most spunlace and needlepunched fabric, are 5603.91 to 5603.94 on the same weight bands. All 27 lines are Free at the general rate; the extra duty depends on the country.

faqs.question: What do HS codes 5603.12, 5603.92 and 5603.94 cover?
faqs.answer: 5603.12 is nonwovens of man-made filaments weighing 25–70 g/m², the largest Chapter 56 import line. 5603.92 is nonwovens of other (staple) fibres of 25–70 g/m², and 5603.94 staple-fibre nonwovens over 150 g/m², including floor-covering underlays. All are Free; China pays 37.5%, and 5603.12, 5603.92 and 5603.94.90 from Canada pay the 50% Section 338 duty.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for rope (nylon, polypropylene, polyester)?
faqs.answer: Textile rope is heading 5607, by fibre. Polyethylene or polypropylene rope is 5607.49: 2.7% if of wide strip, 7% unbraided under 4.8 mm, 9.8¢/kg + 5.3% thicker unbraided, 3.6% braided. Nylon and polyester rope is 5607.50: 3.6% braided, 19.9¢/kg + 10.8% unbraided. Wire rope is not here — it is heading 7312.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for twine and baler twine?
faqs.answer: Twine is heading 5607. Sisal or agave baler twine is 5607.21.00 (Free); polyethylene or polypropylene baler twine is 5607.41 (2.7% or 4%); jute twine is 5607.90.15 (Free). Yarn counts as twine only above a set thickness (Section XI note 3) — for man-made fibres more than 10,000 decitex — so thin cotton or nylon "twine" may be yarn of chapters 52–55.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for felt?
faqs.answer: Heading 5602. Needleloom felt is 5602.10 (12% if laminated, 10.6% otherwise); wool felt that is not coated is 5602.21 (49.5¢/kg + 7.5%); polyester and other felt is 5602.29 (6.3%); coated or impregnated felt is 5602.90. Felt cut into pads, seals or other articles may be classified elsewhere.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for wadding or batting?
faqs.answer: Textile wadding and batting are heading 5601: cotton 3.6%, man-made fibres 6.3%, other 4%. Cellulose (paper) wadding is chapter 48, and sanitary pads, tampons and diapers made of wadding are heading 9619.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for fishing nets and netting?
faqs.answer: Knotted netting of twine, cordage or rope and made-up nets are heading 5608. Made-up fishing nets of man-made fibres are 5608.11 (8%), fish netting 5608.19.10 (8.5%), other man-made netting and nets such as cargo nets 5608.19.20 (5%). Knitted netting is chapter 60, and landing nets for anglers are 9507.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for elastic cord and elastic thread?
faqs.answer: Rubber thread and cord covered with textile is 5604.10.00, at 6.3%. Elastomeric (spandex) filament yarn without rubber is chapter 54, and woven elastic tape is heading 5806.

faqs.question: What are the HS codes for metallic yarn and chenille yarn?
faqs.answer: Metallic yarn is heading 5605: 7.5% for metal-coated or laminated man-made filament or strip, untwisted, and 13.2% for other metalized yarn. Chenille yarn, including polyester chenille, is 5606.00.00 with gimped yarn and loop wale-yarn, at 8%.

faqs.question: What is the tariff on nonwoven fabric from China?
searchedAs: non woven fabric manufacturer in china
faqs.answer: Nonwovens are Free at the general rate, but China pays 25% under Section 301 List 3 (9903.88.03) and 12.5% under the 2026 action (9903.05.31): 37.5% in total. Three staple-fibre lines (5603.92.00.70, 5603.92.00.95, 5603.93.00.90) are excluded from the 25% through November 9, 2026 and pay 12.5%. The IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026.

faqs.question: Do nonwovens and rope from Canada and Mexico pay tariffs under USMCA?
faqs.answer: Goods that qualify under USMCA pay no base rate and no Section 301 duty. To qualify, Chapter 56 goods may not use non-originating man-made fibres or yarn. But Canada's 50% Section 338 duty on 5603.12, 5603.13, 5603.14.90, 5603.92, 5603.94.90 and 5607.50.40 applies even with a USMCA claim.

faqs.question: What are the HTS Chapter 56 tariffs in 2026?
faqs.answer: Base rates run from Free (all nonwovens, sisal baler twine, jute and coir rope) to 14.1% on cotton hammocks and are unchanged since 2025. On top, most countries pay a 10% or 12.5% Section 301 tariff since July 24, 2026; China and Brazil pay 37.5%; Canada 50% on listed nonwovens and cordage; USMCA goods from Mexico pay nothing.

faqs.question: Are twist ties from China subject to antidumping duties?
faqs.answer: Yes. Twist ties from China are under antidumping and countervailing duty orders (A-570-131, C-570-132) that name 5609.00.30.00 and 8309.90.00.00 as their main entry numbers. In 2026 Commerce found that revoking them would likely lead to dumping margins up to 72.96% and subsidies of 111.96%; the ITC is conducting full reviews.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for a hammock?
faqs.answer: Hammocks of knotted cotton netting are 5608.90.23, at 14.1% — the highest ad valorem base rate in Chapter 56; China pays 51.6% in total. Hammocks sewn from woven fabric, like most camping hammocks, are not knotted netting and are classified with other made-up textile articles outside Chapter 56.

faqs.question: How is the country of origin of a nonwoven or rope determined?
faqs.answer: By CBP's textile rules (19 CFR 102.21). A nonwoven or felt is from the country where its web was formed; twine and rope from where the filaments were extruded or the fibres spun; nets from where the netting was made or the net assembled. Cutting, coating or packing elsewhere does not change it, and the origin decides the Section 301 rate.
